subject: history
title: Détente, the Second Cold War and Collapse 1969-91
welcome_lead: From SALT to the fall of the Berlin Wall and the dissolution of the USSR.
meta_desc: A-Level adventure on détente, Reagan's escalation, Gorbachev's reforms and the end of the Cold War.
final_note: You can evaluate why the Cold War ended without a great-power conflict.

concepts.def: Period of reduced superpower tension c.1969-79, associated with Nixon-Kissinger and Brezhnev: SALT I, Helsinki Accords.
Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty signed 26 May 1972, capping ICBMs and SLBMs and including the ABM Treaty.
Final Act of the CSCE: recognition of post-war borders alongside human-rights commitments (Basket III).
Soviet intervention from December 1979 to February 1989; helped end détente and drained Soviet resources.
Reagan's 1983 'Star Wars' missile defence proposal, pressuring Soviet military spending.
Gorbachev's 1985-91 policies of economic restructuring and political openness that loosened the Soviet system.

walkthroughs.body_html: Nixon's opening to China (February 1972) and Moscow visit (May 1972) yielded SALT I and the ABM Treaty. The Helsinki Accords (1 August 1975) embedded human-rights monitoring. SALT II was signed in June 1979 but not ratified. Soviet intervention in Afghanistan (24 December 1979) and the Iranian Revolution shattered the détente consensus.

Reagan branded the USSR an 'evil empire' (1983) and launched SDI. Cruise and Pershing II deployments in Europe and 1983 'Able Archer' brought tension to a peak. Gorbachev became General Secretary in March 1985 and pursued perestroika and glasnost. The INF Treaty (December 1987) eliminated intermediate-range missiles.

The Sinatra Doctrine permitted Eastern European change. Poland's Round Table (April 1989), Hungary's border opening (May 1989) and the fall of the Berlin Wall (9 November 1989) swept communism away. German reunification followed (3 October 1990). The August 1991 coup against Gorbachev failed; the USSR was dissolved on 25 December 1991, with the Belavezha Accords and Alma-Ata Declaration.
